timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only cell trajectory with no projected semantic events; the serial work is in the single agent session.
Single actor probed docs and CLI behavior, abandoned Rust after dependency constraints, implemented Python, installed it, smoke-tested it, and finalized.

parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the clean-room CLI requirement, the ban on source lookup, and the need to deliver a replacement executable matching observed pier behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent delegated docs and CLI probing while also implementing; children also performed implementation work, leaving final deliverable ownership implicit until the parent reclaimed it.
parallel.implementation: The parent and CLI child pursued Rust/Cargo implementations, while the docs child independently produced a Python implementation and install script for the same executable route.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The child installed Python through compile.sh, then the parent found that build route, deleted the Python entry point, restored compile.sh to Cargo, built Rust, and submitted Rust.
parallel.verification: The run performed black-box CLI checks and final smoke tests, but verification occurred after deliverable route churn and against the parent-selected Rust path.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator failed the submitted Rust artifact at 526 of 779 checks; the child Python work was not retained as the final deliverable.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering constraints and CLI behavior surface from docs and normal command probing.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned probing, implementation, install script, final executable replacement, and smoke verification without cross-agent ownership overlap.
serial.implementation: It first attempted a Rust implementation, found offline crate constraints, deleted the Rust path, then implemented pier.py with a fallback parser and precise help/error behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor added compile.sh to install pier.py as executable and kept that route through final artifact packaging.
serial.verification: It ran help, version, config-init, list, and other representative behavior checks, then reran smoke tests after adding the parser fallback.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed the Python artifact at 649 of 779 checks, indicating ordinary implementation gaps remained despite the coherent route.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel understood the clean-room reverse-engineering task and probed the CLI/documentation surface before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and also used normal CLI/documentation probing under the clean-room constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference is visible; the later difference is in workspace ownership and final route selection.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spawned docs_probe and cli_probe while the parent also implemented, creating overlapping implementation and delivery ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation and one actor owned the entire pipeline from probing through delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel split the work but did not isolate final executable ownership; serial kept ownership centralized.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child task messages were delegated through the multi-agent system, and returned implementation results reached the parent but without a stable file/build ownership contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial transferred no inter-agent context and carried decisions directly from probing into implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had cross-agent context and ownership boundaries to reconcile; serial had no cross-agent contract surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel retained the Rust implementation as the final path after parent and child implementations diverged.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial abandoned the Rust implementation after dependency constraints and used a Python implementation instead.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel submitted Rust after reconciliation, while serial submitted Python as a single coherent route.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The docs child completed and returned a Python implementation, and the parent inspected/reconciled it rather than simply ignoring it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; its implementation state was continuously visible to the same actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel paid a result-reconciliation cost after completed child work changed the live deliverable; serial avoided that lifecycle boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The shared workspace contained a child-installed Python executable route and a parent-owned Rust route; the parent then deleted the Python entry point and rewired compile.sh back to Rust.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial added one compile.sh that installed pier.py as executable and kept that install route stable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel experienced a concrete deliverable overwrite and route reversal; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel smoke-tested the rebuilt Rust executable after restoring the Rust build route.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial smoke-tested the installed Python executable after compile.sh installed it.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified locally, but parallel verification followed a late deliverable-route switch while serial verified the same route it had developed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used multiple live agents, hit a thread-limit spawn failure, and closed after reconciling shared-workspace changes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in one actor with no child activity or delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had coordination overhead and late reconciliation; serial spent its budget on one implementation path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations completed and both solutions failed, so there is no discordant pass/fail outcome. Serial nevertheless had materially higher coverage, 649 of 779 versus parallel 526 of 779. The concrete process difference is that parallel submitted a Rust route after competing child Python and parent Rust deliverables collided, while serial kept one Python route after abandoning Rust.
parallel_contributors: Concurrent deliverable ownership caused a child Python executable route to be replaced by the parent's Rust route before final submission.
The final verification window followed late reconciliation of shared workspace state.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one actor responsible for probing, implementation, installation, and final smoke tests.
Serial switched away from unavailable Rust dependencies into a stable Python route.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The final submitted implementations were different languages and likely differed in behavior coverage beyond the coordination issue.
Both solutions retained functional gaps under the hidden evaluator.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
